You are the analytics assistant for Norrland Home, an online furniture and home goods retailer. You have read-only access to the data warehouse. Never estimate numbers you can query. Amounts are in EUR.
which product categories had the biggest drop in revenue in Q3 compared to Q2? this year. net of refunds if that's possible

<parameter=schema>

</parameter>
</function>

sales.orders        (order_id bigint, customer_id bigint, ordered_at timestamptz, status text, channel text)
sales.order_items   (order_id bigint, line_no int, product_id bigint, quantity int, unit_price numeric(12,2), discount numeric(12,2))
sales.refunds       (refund_id bigint, order_id bigint, line_no int, amount numeric(12,2), refunded_at timestamptz)
sales.products      (product_id bigint, sku text, name text, category text, launched_at date)

<tool_call>
<function=warehouse_query>
<parameter=sql>
WITH line_rev AS (
  SELECT p.category,
         date_trunc('quarter', o.ordered_at) AS q,
         oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - oi.discount AS gross,
         COALESCE(r.amount, 0) AS refunded
  FROM sales.order_items oi
  JOIN sales.orders o USING (order_id)
  JOIN sales.products p USING (product_id)
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT order_id, line_no, SUM(amount) AS amount
    FROM sales.refunds
    GROUP BY order_id, line_no
  ) r USING (order_id, line_no)
  WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled'
    AND o.ordered_at >= '2026-04-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2026-10-01'
),
by_cat AS (
  SELECT category,
         SUM(gross - refunded) FILTER (WHERE q = DATE '2026-04-01') AS q2_net,
         SUM(gross - refunded) FILTER (WHERE q = DATE '2026-07-01') AS q3_net
  FROM line_rev
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT category,
       ROUND(q2_net, 2) AS q2_net,
       ROUND(q3_net, 2) AS q3_net,
       ROUND(q3_net - q2_net, 2) AS change,
       ROUND(100 * (q3_net - q2_net) / NULLIF(q2_net, 0), 2) AS change_pct
FROM by_cat
ORDER BY change_pct;

whats the difference between APR and APY? my bank app shows both for the same savings account and I don't get why they're different numbers

They describe the same interest rate, just with and without compounding:

- **APR** (annual percentage rate) is the simple yearly rate. It doesn't count interest earned on interest.
- **APY** (annual percentage yield) is what you actually earn over a year *including* compounding, i.e. interest paid on the interest already credited.

If interest is paid more often than once a year, APY is always a bit higher than APR. The formula is:

APY = (1 + APR / n)^n − 1, where n is how many times per year interest is credited.

Example: 4.00% APR credited monthly (n = 12) gives (1 + 0.04/12)^12 − 1 ≈ **4.07% APY**. On €10,000 that's about €407 after a year instead of €400.

For a savings account, **APY is the number to compare** between banks, because it already includes how often each bank pays interest. (For loans, lenders like to quote APR because it looks smaller.)

Quillstone 5.0 release notes
Released 14 October 2026

Quillstone 5.0 is our biggest update since we moved to local-first storage. It brings a new editor core, faster sync, and a reworked plugin API. Please read the "Breaking changes" section before you update, especially if you use community plugins or self-hosted sync.

Highlights

New editor core
The editor has been rebuilt on a new document model. Large notes (over 50,000 words) now open up to 6x faster, and typing latency in long documents is down from an average of 38 ms to 7 ms on our test machine (MacBook Air M2, 16 GB). Tables can now be edited directly in the live preview, including adding and removing columns with the keyboard.

Faster sync
Quillstone Sync now transfers only the changed blocks of a note instead of the whole file. In our tests with a vault of 12,000 notes, a full initial sync took 4 min 10 s instead of 11 min 30 s. Conflict handling has been improved: instead of creating a "conflicted copy" file, Quillstone now merges non-overlapping edits automatically and shows a side-by-side view for overlapping ones.

Canvas 2.0
Canvases can now contain live queries, embedded PDFs with annotations, and groups that can be collapsed. Exported canvases keep their layout in the new .qcanvas format.

Tasks
Tasks now support recurring due dates ("every 2nd Tuesday"), start dates and dependencies. The Tasks view can be grouped by note, tag, due date or priority.

Breaking changes

Plugin API v3
Plugins written for the v2 API will not load in 5.0 until their authors update them. The main changes are:
- The editor is now accessed through app.editor.view instead of app.workspace.activeEditor.
- File events are now asynchronous and must be awaited.
- The old settings tab API has been removed; plugins must use the new SettingsPanel component.
When you start 5.0, plugins that are not yet compatible are disabled automatically and listed under Settings > Plugins > Needs update. Your plugin data and settings are kept. At release, 64 of the 100 most-installed community plugins had published a v3-compatible version. A compatibility list is maintained at quillstone.example/plugins/compat.

WebDAV sync
WebDAV sync has moved from the core app into an official plugin ("WebDAV Sync"), so that it can be updated independently. On first start, 5.0 will offer to install the plugin and migrate your existing WebDAV settings. If you skip this step, WebDAV sync stops until the plugin is installed. Servers that do not support the PROPFIND Depth: infinity header (for example some NAS models) need the new option "Shallow listing" enabled; this is detected automatically during migration.

Minimum system requirements
- Windows 10 version 21H2 or later
- macOS 12 Monterey or later
- Ubuntu 22.04 or comparable distributions (glibc 2.35+)
- iOS 16 / Android 10 or later
32-bit Windows is no longer supported.

Removed features
- The legacy "Classic" theme has been removed. Notes using Classic-only CSS snippets may look different.
- The Markdown export option "Wikilinks as plain text" has been replaced by the new export profiles.

Other improvements
- Search is up to 3x faster for vaults with more than 10,000 notes.
- New command palette with fuzzy search and recent commands.
- Daily notes can now be created from a template per weekday.
- Images pasted from the clipboard are converted to WebP by default (can be changed in Settings > Files).
- Better screen reader support in the sidebar and settings.
- Fixed: links to headings with emoji were not resolved.
- Fixed: on Android, the keyboard sometimes covered the last line of a note.
- Fixed: very long file names caused sync errors on Windows.

Updating
Quillstone keeps a full backup of your vault configuration (.quillstone folder) before the update, in .quillstone/backup-4.x. To go back to 4.x, install version 4.9.3 from the downloads page and restore that folder. Notes themselves are not changed by the update.

Short version: **yes, two things in 5.0 affect your setup directly**, but neither touches your notes, and both can be handled during the update.

**1. WebDAV sync becomes a plugin**
- WebDAV is no longer built in; it's now the official "WebDAV Sync" plugin.
- On first start, 5.0 offers to install it and migrate your settings. **Don't skip that step**, or sync stops until you install it.
- If your server is a NAS that doesn't support `PROPFIND` with `Depth: infinity`, a "Shallow listing" option is needed. The migration should detect this, but check it if sync acts up.

**2. Plugin API v3: older plugins stop loading**
- Plugins built for the v2 API are disabled automatically and listed under *Settings > Plugins > Needs update*. Their data and settings are kept.
- At release, only 64 of the top 100 community plugins had a compatible version. Check your plugins against the list at quillstone.example/plugins/compat **before** updating; if one you rely on isn't there yet, it's worth waiting.

**Smaller things that might affect you**
- The "Classic" theme is gone, so CSS snippets written for it may look different.
- The export option "Wikilinks as plain text" has been replaced by export profiles.
- Pasted images are now saved as WebP by default.
- 32-bit Windows is no longer supported, and the minimum versions are now Windows 10 21H2 / macOS 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 / iOS 16 / Android 10.

**What's new and good**
- A new editor core: much faster with long notes, and tables can be edited directly in live preview.
- Quillstone Sync sends only changed blocks and merges non-overlapping edits instead of creating conflicted copies (though that's their own sync service, not WebDAV).
- Canvas 2.0, recurring tasks with start dates and dependencies, faster search, and a new command palette.

**If something goes wrong:** the update backs up your config to `.quillstone/backup-4.x`. You can reinstall 4.9.3 and restore that folder.

My suggestion: check the plugin compatibility list first, then update and accept the WebDAV migration.

what's actually the difference between dew point and humidity? which one tells me if it's going to feel muggy

**Dew point** is the better one for "muggy".

- **Relative humidity** (%) tells you how close the air is to saturation *at its current temperature*. Because warm air can hold much more water than cold air, the same percentage means very different things: 90% on a 5 °C morning feels damp and chilly, while 90% at 30 °C is oppressive.
- **Dew point** (°C/°F) is the temperature the air would have to cool to for dew to form. It depends only on how much water vapour is actually in the air, not on the temperature, so it tracks how sticky it feels directly.

Rough guide for how it feels:

| Dew point | Feels |
|---|---|
| below 10 °C (50 °F) | dry, comfortable |
| 10–15 °C (50–60 °F) | pleasant |
| 16–18 °C (61–65 °F) | getting humid |
| 19–21 °C (66–70 °F) | muggy |
| above 21 °C (70 °F) | oppressive |

That's also why relative humidity is often highest early in the morning, when it's coolest, even on days that only feel sticky in the afternoon. If you tell me where you are, I can check today's dew point for you.
